title: Волосы в салате и штраф для Сени  (Hairs in the Salad and a Fine for Senya)

segments.t: Quoting Sun Tzu on killing an enemy with a borrowed knife, Max plants Senya's two red hairs onto a salad plate headed for the dining room. When the disgusted guest shows the red hairs to Vika and pours salt over the dish, Vika makes Senya pay for the replacement.
Воспользуйся чужим ножом, чтобы убить врага.
Простите, я не понимаю, как это получилось.
Чтобы вы этот же не принесли.
Let's walk back through the scene line by line.
Воспользуйся чужим ножом, чтобы убить врага.
'Kill the enemy with a borrowed knife.' Max anchors the line on 'to take advantage of', while 'enemy' completes the thought.
'Young man, may I have a word with you?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'young' before landing on 'you'. Max answers right away.
'Yes, how can I help you?' The grammar packs 'yes' and 'I'm listening' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'To be precise, two red hairs.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'definitely' before landing on 'hair'.
'Is this some kind of special promotion?' Notice how Russian expresses 'this' and 'rally' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Vika answers right away.
'Buy one hair and get the second one free.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'second' and finishing on 'for free'.
Простите, я не понимаю, как это получилось.
'Forgive me, I have no idea how that happened.' Notice how Russian expresses 'forgive' and 'worked out' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'We are sincerely sorry.' The meaning hinges on 'we' working together with 'to regret' in spoken Russian. Max answers right away.
'We will replace your dish immediately.' Notice how Russian expresses 'we' and 'to replace' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Чтобы вы этот же не принесли.
'Just to make sure you do not bring back the exact same plate.' Vika anchors the line on 'so that', while 'brought' completes the thought.
'Once again, please accept my apologies.' In Russian, the idea of 'else' flows naturally into 'forgiveness' without extra filler words. Vika answers right away.
'You are going to pay for this dish yourself.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'will you?' before landing on 'to pay'.
'The salad is coming out of your paycheck.' Max brings out the contrast between 'salad' and 'behind' in a few short words. Let's hear the full exchange one more time at natural speed.

Чтобы вы этот же не принесли.
That wraps up this scene as max slips Senya's two red hairs into a guest's salad to spark a feud, resulting in Vika docking the cost of the ruined dish from Senya's pay. See you next time!
